videos.why: The most famous name of the three set against the viewer's own salary, with a one-line payoff ('before breakfast') that answers the hook; moved above rank's 7.6 for the hook and the payoff.
strengths: Ronaldo, a global name, on a money-scale story
The hook denies a belief the viewer holds about their own pay
The payoff is one clear, visual line, with the figures on the plate
risks: The per-minute beat is a text card (a headline scene)
The week beat stacks a calendar, a cash pile and a player close together

videos.why: A surprise most viewers don't know (M a year from a 00M deal) and a sourced turn (sponsors pay far more); slightly below Ronaldo because the name is less known outside baseball.
strengths: Real, sourced figures from NBC and Forbes
Clear contrast in the turn: 25M from sponsors against M from the team
risks: The 'his idea' reason is carried mostly by the voice
The billboard is cropped a little at the payoff

videos.why: A big, famous company and a fair mechanism, but the $377B figure is never spoken, and 'cash waits for a sale' is closer to what viewers already know.
strengths: A huge sourced figure, with a crossed-out 'wasted' cover
The turn shows a market crash and a SALE sign
risks: The topic is closer to textbook than the other two
The interest figure rests on an assumed 4% rate
